llm.summary: The skill appears intended for lecture-note generation, but it persistently duplicates full PDF contents and allows downstream local indexing without a clear opt-in or redaction step.

dimensions.detail: Using PDF extraction tools and writing notes into a course repository is coherent, but the hardcoded Polito path and generic triggers may cause writes in a broader or less explicit context than some users expect.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains only Markdown metadata/instructions and JSON metadata; no bundled executable scripts, remote payload retrieval, or install-time code were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires zero information loss, verbatim preservation of potentially sensitive PDF content, bilingual copies, backups, and downstream local RAG indexing, but does not require user confirmation for sensitive PDFs or indexing.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates persistent Markdown outputs and .bak files and states that generated notes will be picked up by an existing daily local-rag indexing run; it does not install persistence itself, but it expands retention and searchability of source content.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, converting Polito lecture PDFs into Italian and English Markdown notes, matches the core file-reading and note-writing behavior.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing if your PDFs may contain personal, confidential, unpublished, or regulated information. Use it only for lecture material you are comfortable storing as plaintext notes, backups, and searchable local RAG entries, and consider disabling indexing or adding a redaction/confirmation step for sensitive documents.
llm.findings:
[SQP-3] expected: The bilingual IT+EN output is central to the stated Polito notes purpose, so this is a product-scope constraint rather than a security concern by itself.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Generic trigger terms such as notes, materia, and lezione are broader than necessary for a PDF conversion workflow and could cause ambiguous activation, though the input section still expects a PDF and course name.
[SSD-3] expected: Comprehensive note generation is purpose-aligned, but the artifact explicitly preserves all PDF content, including sensitive or personal data, into persistent Markdown and downstream indexing without a consent gate.
[RA2] unexpected: I did not find evidence that this skill establishes cron jobs, startup scripts, or its own cross-session persistence; it only references an existing local-rag daily cron.
[T09] expected: The plaintext duplication and indexing concern is supported by the artifact: two Markdown files, possible .bak files, and local-rag pickup are all described, with no redaction, retention, or index-exclusion controls.
